samples.summary: Increase/Decrease Decimals becomes a visual no-op for cells whose effective format is explicitly `nf: 'plain'` — the new pinning writes `'plain'` back over the `'number'` the step needs
samples.evidence: `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4352-4359) sets `patch.nf = 'number'` and passes `{ defaultKeys: ['nf'] }` when the active cell's `nf` is falsy **or** `'plain'`. In the cell path, `collectStyleValuesToPin` (sheet.ts:3836-3844) pins any effective value that differs from the patch: for a cell whose effective `nf` is the explicit string `'plain'`, `value ('plain') !== patch.nf ('number')`, so `keep = { nf: 'plain' }` is written back at cell level *after* the patch lands (sheet.ts:3802-3804). The stepped `dp` is therefore stored but never rendered — `formatValue` returns the raw value for `nf === 'plain'` (format.ts:205-207) — and the cell is permanently pinned to `plain` at cell level. Explicit `nf:'plain'` is common: xlsx import emits it (`packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-styles.ts:254` for numFmtId 49 and :294 for `@`), the toolbar 'Plain' item applies it (`packages/frontend/src/components/formatting-toolbar.tsx:417/843` → `applyStyle({nf:'plain'})`), and `DefaultResetStylePatch` contains `nf:'plain'` (sheet.ts:163). The same hole exists on the column/row/all paths via `withoutSetDefaults` (sheet.ts:3745/3762/3776), which drops `nf` whenever the layer already holds one — including `'plain'`. Every new test in `decimals.test.ts` uses `nf: undefined`, so this case is untested.

samples.summary: Pinning materializes inherited column/row/sheet formats onto individual cells, permanently breaking style inheritance for those cells
samples.evidence: `collectStyleValuesToPin` resolves the *effective* style (sheet.ts:3836) and then `setRangeStyle` writes those values onto the cell itself (`await this.setStyle(parseRef(sref), keep)`, sheet.ts:3803). A cell that merely *inherited* `nf: 'percent'` from a column/row/sheet layer now carries an explicit cell-level `nf: 'percent'`. After a single Increase Decimals over a wide selection, changing the column's number format no longer affects those cells (cell level wins in `resolveEffectiveStyle`, sheet.ts:917), and undo of the decimal step does not necessarily unwind the pinned cell writes. The test at decimals.test.ts:600-616 asserts only that the pinned render is right, not that inheritance survives.

samples.summary: Empty cells in the selection are not pinned, so the appended `nf: 'number'` patch silently overrides the format they inherit
samples.evidence: `collectStyleValuesToPin` iterates `store.getGrid(range)` (sheet.ts:3828), which only yields *populated* cells. The range patch appended at sheet.ts:3800 carries `nf:'number'` and sits above the sheet/column/row layers, so an empty cell in the selection that inherits `nf:'percent'` from a column style loses it — silently, and only visibly later when the user types a number into it. The doc comment at sheet.ts:4353-4357 claims the neighbouring format is kept, which holds only for cells that already have content.

samples.summary: `withoutSetDefaults` compares the patch only against the same layer, not the effective style, so column/row steps still override formats inherited from lower layers
samples.evidence: `withoutSetDefaults(style, colStyle, defaultKeys)` (sheet.ts:171-191, used at 3745/3762/3776) drops a default key only when *that layer* already sets it. For a column selection where `nf: 'percent'` lives on the sheet style (a lower-priority layer), the column patch still writes `nf:'number'`, which then wins over the sheet's percent for the whole column — exactly the conversion `defaultKeys` exists to prevent. Same for a row selection over a column that carries `nf`, since row styles override column styles (`resolveEffectiveStyle`, sheet.ts:917).

samples.summary: Decrease at the floor on a cell with an explicit `dp` but no `nf` adds `nf: 'number'`, visibly changing the display of a press that should do nothing
samples.evidence: The no-op guard at sheet.ts:4318 requires `!explicitDp`, so a cell with an explicit `dp` (e.g. `dp:0` with `nf` absent, or `dp` left behind by `resetRangeStyleToDefault`, whose reset patch sets `nf:'plain'` but never clears `dp`) skips it. `clamped` is then true, `target` is 0, the unset branch is skipped (`!clamped` fails), and `setRangeStyle({dp: 0, nf: 'number'})` runs — turning a raw `1234` into `1,234` on a Decrease that had nothing to drop.

samples.summary: `unsetRangeStyleValues` persists empty style objects for sheet/column/row layers instead of clearing them
samples.evidence: `omitStyleKeys` returns `{}` (truthy) when the removed keys were the layer's only keys (range-styles.ts:64-76). The patch loop drops such patches (sheet.ts:4621), but the sheet/column/row branches write the empty object straight through: `this.sheetStyle = next; await this.store.setSheetStyle(next)` (4579-4580), `this.colStyles.set(col, next)` (4591), `this.rowStyles.set(row, next)` (4604). Afterwards `resolveEffectiveStyle` no longer short-circuits (`if (!s && !c && ...)`, sheet.ts:916) and `getStyle` returns `{}` instead of `undefined`, and an empty `colStyles`/`sheetStyle` entry is persisted to the document forever.

samples.summary: A cell whose style becomes empty is deleted via `isEmptyCell`, which ignores the spill fields `compactCell` now preserves
samples.evidence: `compactCell` was changed to carry `spillRows/spillCols/spillAnchor/spillBlocked`, but `isEmptyCell` (style-mutation.ts:48-52) still only looks at value/formula/style. In `unsetRangeStyleValues` (sheet.ts:4632-4634) and `setStyle` (sheet.ts:3715-3719) a spill ghost whose computed value is the empty string and whose style has just been emptied is judged empty and deleted, dropping the `spillAnchor` link the calculator relies on.

samples.summary: `decimalsInValue` counts characters after the first dot in *any* string, so text values yield a bogus starting precision for the decimal step
samples.evidence: `decimalsInValue` does no numeric check: `'abc.defgh'` → 5, `'1.2.3'` → 3, `'2026-02-18 00:00:00'` → 0 but `'v1.2.3'` → 3. `getActiveDecimalState` (sheet.ts:4286) calls it on `cell?.v` unconditionally, so with a text active cell (common for a column selection whose row 1 is a header, since `selectColumn` sets `activeCell = {r:1,c:col}`) `valueDp` is arbitrary and drives both the reported `dp` and the `target === valueDp` unset decision at sheet.ts:4334. `selectionRendersAt` guards with `isNaN(Number(value))` (sheet.ts:4379); `getActiveDecimalState` does not.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. changeDecimals (sheet.ts:4352-4359) upgrades falsy-or-'plain' nf to 'number' and passes defaultKeys:['nf']. collectStyleValuesToPin (sheet.ts:3838-3844) has no exemption for the literal 'plain': effective nf 'plain' !== patch nf 'number', so keep={nf:'plain'} is written back via setStyle AFTER the patch lands (sheet.ts:3800-3804), and normalizeStylePatch (range-styles.ts:19-24) preserves 'plain'. formatValue returns the raw value for nf==='plain' (format.ts:205-207), so the stepped dp is stored but never rendered and the cell is left pinned to plain at cell level. The column/row/all paths have the same hole: withoutSetDefaults (sheet.ts:181-189) deletes nf whenever the layer already holds one, including 'plain' (sheet.ts:3745/3762/3776). Explicit nf:'plain' is reachable from xlsx import (xlsx-styles.ts:254, 294), the toolbar Plain item (formatting-toolbar.tsx:243 via 417/843) and DefaultResetStylePatch (sheet.ts:163). No test covers it — grep for 'plain' in packages/sheets/test/sheet/decimals.test.ts returns no matches. Real, user-visible logic bug (Increase/Decrease Decimals silently does nothing on plain-formatted cells) squarely in the correctness lane.

A cell that merely *inherited* `nf: 'percent'` from a column/row/sheet layer now carries an explicit cell-level `nf: 'percent'`. After a single Increase Decimals over a wide selection, changing the column's number format no longer affects those cells (cell level wins in `resolveEffectiveStyle`, sheet.ts:917), and undo of the decimal step does not necessarily unwind the pinned cell writes. mergedFrom.summary: `withoutSetDefaults` compares the patch only against the same layer, not the effective style, so column/row steps still override formats inherited from lower layers
mergedFrom.evidence: `withoutSetDefaults(style, colStyle, defaultKeys)` (sheet.ts:171-191, used at 3745/3762/3776) drops a default key only when *that layer* already sets it. For a column selection where `nf: 'percent'` lives on the sheet style (a lower-priority layer), the column patch still writes `nf:'number'`, which then wins over the sheet's percent for the whole column — exactly the conversion `defaultKeys` exists to prevent. Same for a row selection over a column that carries `nf`, since row styles override column styles (`resolveEffectiveStyle`, sheet.ts:917).

verdict.reason: The pinning code exists as quoted, but the claimed harm is contradicted by the surrounding mechanism. (a) resolveEffectiveStyle merges sheet -> col -> row -> RANGE -> cell (sheet.ts:917), so the range layer already outranks column/row/sheet. (b) In the cell-selection branch the very same call does addRangeStylePatch(range, style) with the unmodified patch (sheet.ts:3800) — withoutSetDefaults is applied only in the column/row/all branches (3745/3762/3776). The only caller that passes defaultKeys is changeDecimals with patch.nf='number' (sheet.ts:4351-4359), and nf:'number' is never pruned since DefaultStyleValues.nf==='plain' (style-mutation.ts:19-31, 284-306); the only early-out in addRangeStylePatch requires stylesEqual (style-mutation.ts:134-148), i.e. an equal nf patch already shadows the column. So the column/row/sheet nf is shadowed for every cell in the selection by the range patch regardless of pinning. Pinning writes only keys in defaultKeys (sheet.ts:3838-3844), which are exactly the keys the range patch carries, so it severs no inheritance link that the step had not already shadowed; it only restores the rendered value (test decimals.test.ts:596-612). (c) No overwrite: when the cell already owns the key, effective[key]===cell.s[key], so the write-back is a no-op, and later explicit range styling still reaches such cells via applyStylePatchToExistingCells (sheet.ts:1978-2012). (d) The undo sub-claim is wrong: the pinned setStyle calls sit inside beginBatch/endBatch (sheet.ts:3737, 3802-3804, 3807), which store.ts:275-284 defines as a single undo step and yorkie-store.ts:1163-1189/1199-1206 implements as one doc.update reverted by history.undo(). The behavior is also the documented design (docs/design/sheets/sheet-style.md:263-268). No wrong condition, crash, data loss, or broken invariant under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: changeDecimals steps from the raw stored `dp`, so a NaN `dp` propagates into a new write instead of being clamped
finding.evidence: `const stepped = Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES);` uses `dp` straight from `getActiveDecimalState()`, which returns `style.dp` untouched (sheet.ts:4184). The delta clamps only at format time (`clampDecimals` in formatValue). If the stored `dp` is `NaN` — exactly the hostile/imported value the new clamp exists for — `stepped` is `NaN`, `NaN < 0` is false so `clamped` is false, `target === valueDp` is false, and the function reaches `setRangeStyle({ dp: NaN, ... })`, persisting `NaN` into the style layer. `unsetRangeStyleValues` also can never match it (`NaN !== NaN` → 'conflict'). Every subsequent Increase/Decrease press stays at `NaN` — the control is permanently stuck for that selection — and a NaN is not JSON/CRDT representable, so the value that reaches collaborators is undefined behaviour. Applying `clampDecimals(dp, 2)` before stepping would fix it.

verdict.reason: The finding's central premise is factually wrong in this tree. `getActiveDecimalState()` does NOT return `style.dp` untouched: sheet.ts:4293-4299 returns `dp: clampDecimals(style.dp, rendersRaw ? valueDp : 2)`, and `clampDecimals` (format.ts:22-30) returns the fallback whenever `!Number.isFinite(dp)`, so a stored `NaN` becomes `valueDp` or `2`. Both fallbacks are finite integers (`decimalsInValue`, format.ts:133-139, returns 0 or a digit count; otherwise literal `2`), and the other return paths (sheet.ts:4303, 4305) also yield `valueDp`/`2`. Hence `stepped = Math.min(dp + delta, MAX_DECIMAL_PLACES)` at sheet.ts:4317 cannot be NaN, `setRangeStyle({ dp: NaN })` is unreachable via this path, and the buttons cannot wedge. Callers only pass ±1 (spreadsheet.ts:536, 546), so `delta` is not a NaN source either. An existing regression test, decimals.test.ts:560-573, asserts precisely the scenario the reviewer claims is broken (stored `dp: NaN` + `nf: 'number'` steps to 3). The cited evidence location (sheet.ts:4184) contains no such code. Ground: not-present.

finding.summary: selectionRendersAt's new format-aware check makes Decrease reach a write that clobbers a neighbour's number format with `nf: 'number'`
finding.evidence: `if (!nf || nf === 'plain') patch.nf = 'number';` takes `nf` from the ACTIVE cell only, and `setRangeStyle` → `applyStylePatchToExistingCells` (sheet.ts:1978-1991) writes conflicting keys onto each existing cell's own style. So when the active cell has no `nf` and a neighbour has `nf: 'percent'`/`'currency'`, one Decrease silently converts that neighbour to `nf: 'number'` — '0.5' stops reading '50.00%' and reads '0.5'. This delta newly widens the path: `selectionRendersAt` now uses `renderedDecimals`, so selections that previously short-circuited at line 4203 (e.g. plain '12' beside a percent cell storing '12', both 0 decimals by value) now fall through to the write. The new test at decimals.test.ts:504-517 exercises exactly this case and asserts only `dp === 0`, so the lost `nf: 'percent'` on B1 is not caught.

verdict.reason: The finding's central premise — that `patch.nf = 'number'` is written through a plain `setRangeStyle` that overrides each cell's own format — is not what the code does. `sheet.ts:4359` calls `this.setRangeStyle(patch, { defaultKeys: ['nf'] })`. For cell-range selections, `setRangeStyle` first calls `collectStyleValuesToPin(range, style, defaultKeys)` (sheet.ts:3795-3799, implemented at 3818-3850) which records each populated cell's *effective* `nf` (resolved through sheet/col/row/range layers via `resolveEffectiveStyle`, sheet.ts:907-918) whenever it differs from the patch; then after `addRangeStylePatch` and `applyStylePatchToExistingCells` write `nf:'number'`, the pinned values are written back at the cell level (sheet.ts:3802-3804), which is the highest-precedence layer (sheet.ts:917). For column/row/all selections, `withoutSetDefaults` (sheet.ts:171-191) drops the defaulted key when the layer already sets it. So a neighbour holding `nf:'percent'`/`'currency'` is not converted to `'number'`. This is asserted directly by decimals.test.ts:575-594 (`getStyle({r:1,c:2}).nf === 'percent'` and B1 still renders as a percentage after a Decrease from a format-less active cell) and decimals.test.ts:596-612 for the column-inherited case. In the test the reviewer cites (decimals.test.ts:502-517), B1's own style is `{dp:1, nf:'percent'}`, so the same pin restores it. The widened `selectionRendersAt` (sheet.ts:4374-4394) does let more selections fall through to the write, but the write it reaches is format-preserving, so the claimed silent format clobber/data loss does not occur.
